item.title: 26SSEIT22001-Subscription of 3 Consumer Data Statara Licenses
item.description:
Dept. of Social Svcs/Human Resources Administration | Procurement | Award | $99K | Vendor: Compulink Technologies Inc

The Statara consumer dataset provides information on over 5.5 million adult New Yorkers. This serves as a single data source that provides far broader coverage than PEU can get from various partner agency sources. Having this broad coverage is critical during emergencies and also helps PEU reach New Yorkers who have fewer existing touchpoints with the City. Without the consumer file in question, PEUs efforts to reach out to underserved New Yorkers, especially during and after emergencies, will be greatly impaired. This procurement is therefore necessary for continuation of critical agency functions, a Mayoral Priority, and directly related to public health and safety. An annual license for a consumer detail analytics file install, including updated and refreshed cell phone contact data available for NYC to house in your internal analytics database. This will include NYC residents that may be overlooked on traditional publicly available and privately sourced data sets. An annual license for consumer details to house inside of your separately licensed CRM database.

item.description:

The Department of Youth and Community Development (DYCD), as the designated Community Action Agency for New York City, administers the federal Community Services Block Grant (CSBG) program to combat poverty and provide services that empower low-income individuals and families to achieve self-sufficiency. To maximize the impact of CSBG funding, DYCD targets funds to low-income neighborhoods designated as Neighborhood Development Areas (NDAs). The NDA Initiative promotes community-level engagement to ensure that services address the most pressing needs within each community. Programs use a strength-based approach, partnering with participants to build upon existing assets and capacities to achieve personal and community goals. Given the specialized nature of these services and the need for continuity and responsiveness to local community conditions, DYCD seeks approval to use the Negotiated Acquisition method in accordance with PPB Rule §3-04(b)(2)(i)(D). This approach allows the agency to negotiate directly with qualified community-based organizations (CBOs) that have demonstrated experience, trust, and engagement within their respective NDAs.

item.description:
Youth and Community Development | Procurement | Award | $348K | Vendor: Asian Americans for Equality Inc.

Providers deliver comprehensive services for immigrant families living in low income neighborhoods throughout the city of New York. The goal of the comprehensive services to immigrant families is to:  identify the complex and multiple needs of newly-arrived limited English proficiency families, and, in collaboration with a network of community-based providers, ensure that they gain access to services that help them become self-sufficient and prosper, help each enrolled family build the self-advocacy skills and gain the knowledge to enable them to address specific challenges and navigate key systems that impact their lives (for example, the education, healthcare, housing, benefits, tax, workplace, and legal and immigration systems)

item.title: COMPASS Programs in Public Schools - Middle
item.description:
Youth and Community Development | Procurement | Award | $3.5M | Vendor: The Aster Initiative Inc

COMPASS and SONYC is one of DYCD's largest programs, with over 820 programs collectively throughout the five boroughs. Families rely on these programs to provide elementary and middle school students, during after school hours, summer and on holidays, programing which includes educational support, recreation, enrichment, and cultural activities to support and strengthen the overall development of our youth. Programs are offered at no cost to youth and are purposefully located in public and private schools, community centers, religious institutions, public housing and parks recreational facilities throughout the City to help families find a place that best fits their youth's needs.
